originals.citation: Gable, P. A., & Harmon-Jones, E. (2008). Approach-motivated positive affect reduces breadth of attention. Psychological Science, 19(5), 476-482. Study 2.

quote: Seminal work by Gable and Harmon-Jones (... 2008 ... Study 2) found that pictures of desserts narrowed attentional breadth relative to pictures of rocks. ... we conducted a registered conceptual replication
notes: @domachowska2016 is an earlier RRR of the same finding, cited but the title and abstract frame Gable & Harmon-Jones 2008 as the replicated study.
